section_2.content: Formally define π (Pi) as the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter (C/d = π). Explain that no matter how large or small the circle is, this ratio remains constant. Emphasize that it is an irrational number.
section_2.example: Visualize a tiny coin, a dinner plate, and a giant Ferris wheel side-by-side. If you divide the circumference of each by its diameter, you get the same 'magic' number: 3.14159...

section_3.title: Historical Evolution: The Method of Exhaustion

section_3.example: Visual: A square inside a circle, evolving into a hexagon, then a 12-sided shape, and finally a 96-sided polygon, 'squeezing' the circle until its boundaries are perfectly matched.

section_4.title: Modern Perspectives and Wrap-up
section_4.content: Transition from ancient geometry to the digital era. Explain why we care today: precision in engineering, GPS, and supercomputer stress-testing. Summarize that π is not just a number, but a bridge between geometry and the infinite.
section_4.example: A smartphone navigating a delivery robot to your front door uses the value of π to calculate exact circular turning paths, showing how an ancient concept powers modern technology.

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
